pageCache.pageTitle: Values - Grove Road Primary School		 		Grove Road Primary SchoolValues - Grove Road Primary School
pageCache.text:
Values
Skills and Values
School life is an important journey but is not just about the academic subjects. Children need to learn key life skills and values in order to become healthy and respectful citizens. All parts of school life are equally important and thus we have chosen our key skills and values to underpin all experiences at Grove Road School.
Each Half-term we will explore one of these skills & values in more detail through assemblies and activities. They also form part of our behaviour policy and the expectations of behaviours for everyone at Grove Road School.
Autumn 1
Initiative
This is when we demonstrate our independent skills and know when to just get on and do!
We show that we can organise ourselves appropriately and be ready to learn. We can use our collaborative skills and support one another when it is appropriate to do so.
We may have ideas that we will share and explore with one another. We may demonstrate leadership skills and the ability to take on new things and ideas with confidence and just go for it!
Autumn 2
Resilience
This is when we show that we never give up!
Even when we are faced with challenges or something new we give it 100% and show stamina and endurance.
We can try different ways of doing things always ensuring that we try to improve or better ourselves.
We do not retaliate and show real strength of character. We persevere, if something is worth doing we do it well!
Spring 1
Empathy
This is when we understand that there are consequences to the choices that we make.
We respect each other’s feelings and situations or circumstances.
We care about each other and show kindness to each other.
We can reflect on our actions and behaviour choices and always want to do better.
We want to help each other and ourselves to be better citizens.
We always show good manners and politeness.
Spring 2
Self-confidence
This is when we try new things and push ourselves to be better.
We always give new initiatives and things a go – we never know – we might enjoy it!
We can be risk-takers and learn outside of our comfort zones.
We can stand up for ourselves and are always trying to improve and be a better version of ourselves.
Summer 1
Curiosity
This is when we show an interest in our learning and the world in which we live.
We show this by extending our learning, maybe by furthering our learning or interests at home, in our own time.
We can extend our learning and understanding by reading similar books, stories by the same authors, exploring a country further, researching a science topic, the list is endless!
We show a real thirst for knowledge and understanding of the time and world in which we live.
Summer 2
Creativity
This is when we want to inspire and show off our creative side when learning.
We might want to add a bit more, add some personal flair or just be creative with what we have.
We want to be unique and stand out.
We want to show another side to learning and enjoy diversity.
We want to share our imaginative side and not to be afraid of thinking differently!

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome - Grove Road Primary School		 		Grove Road Primary SchoolWelcome - Grove Road Primary School
pageCache.text:
Welcome
I am very pleased to welcome you to Grove Road Primary School – our family school where all are equally valued.
Grove Road is a small school and we see that as one of our strengths. We know our children well. We know their personalities, their interests, what they are good at and where they need our help. We want every child to feel that they belong here and to know that there are adults in school who believe in them.
We have high expectations for our children, both in their learning and in the people they are becoming. We want them to be curious about the world, to ask questions, think hard, try new things and be creative. We want them to experience success, but also to learn that getting things wrong, finding something difficult and having another go are an important part of learning.
As children grow through Grove Road, we want them to become more confident in themselves and more independent. We want them to find their voice and learn how to use it well. Just as importantly, we want them to listen to others, show empathy and understand that other people may see and experience the world differently. We give children opportunities to make choices, take initiative, contribute to school life and see that their actions matter.
Our 18-place Autism Spectrum Condition Centre is an important part of Grove Road. The children in the Centre are part of our school family and share in the life and experiences of the school, while receiving specialist teaching and support based on their individual needs. The Centre adds a great deal to our school and to children’s understanding of difference, inclusion and one another.
Parents and carers know their children better than anyone, so working closely with families matters to us. We want you to know what your child is learning, to feel comfortable talking to us and to be involved in their education. When home and school know and trust one another, we can do much more for our children.
Our promise is that children will leave Grove Road with strong foundations for whatever comes next. We want them to leave us curious, creative, resilient, compassionate and confident – knowing who they are, believing in what they can become and understanding that they can make a difference.
I am very proud to be Headteacher of Grove Road. I am proud of our children, our staff and our families, and of the school we continue to build together.
If you are considering Grove Road for your child, please come and visit us. Meet our children and staff, walk around the school and see what Grove Road is like for yourself. We would be very pleased to welcome you.
Mrs Grace BeckfordHeadteacher

All Hounslow schools have a similar approach to meeting the needs of students with Special Educational Needs and are supported by the Local Authority to ensure that all students, regardless of their specific needs, make the best possible progress in school. All schools are supported to be as inclusive as possible, with the needs of students with a Special Educational Need/s being met in a mainstream setting wherever possible, where families want this to happen.

pageCache.text:
Governors
The chair of the Grove Road Primary School governing board is Ken Emerson who was appointed by the local authority.
The main role for governors is to support the Headteacher and staff. Governors help to set and reach targets and to strive for excellence. Governors are essential to the work of the school and are legally responsible for it. They are not however, involved in the day to day running of the school.
The two key documents used for this are the School Development Plan and the Summary Self Evaluation Form (SEF). The SDP sets out our strategic plan for the school, with targets that everyone works towards, and the SEF sets out how well the school is doing and where we aim to make improvements.
Governors have a duty and focus on:
The full Governing Body meets at least once every half-term. At this meeting the Headteacher reports to all governors about learning, progress, staffing, financial and premises matters. No committees are held.
There are several categories of Governor, appointed by different groups that have an interest in the school including from the community, parents and staff.
An associate member on a governing board is appointed to provide specific skills and expertise to the board. They are not governors and do not have voting rights on the full governing board.
The governors are committed to providing an excellent environment for all pupils to enjoy during their time at our school.
If you would like any additional information about our School Governors, please ask for information from the office.
To contact the Chair of Governors, please contact the school office using office@groveroad.hounslow.sch.uk with emails clearly marked for the attention of the Chair.
Ken Emerson – Chair of Governors
I am the Chair of the Governing Board and Local Authority Governor. My interest in becoming a Governor started when my children were at Primary School and I was a volunteer on a school trip to the British Museum. I enjoyed being part of the School Community so much I wanted to give something back.
I have been a Governor in different schools for over ten years and successfully gone through three Ofsted Inspections. Grove Road is particularly special with its family feel, commitment to inclusion, and wanting the best for all pupils.
My professional background means I can bring in skills around safeguarding, recruitment, strategic thinking and meeting targets. All necessary things to ensure the Governing board and school are well supported.
As a local resident of 40 years, I am proud to be part of the local community.
Hardeep Walia – Vice Chair of Governors
I have lived in Hounslow all my adult life, now that I have more time, I feel its import to give back to the local community. I got the opportunity to become a governor during covid; it’s something I have been privileged to have had the opportunity to do.
I get asked why primary and not secondary school and why Grove Road. The answer is quite simple.
In the words of Whitney Houston,
‘I believe the children are our future, teach them well and let them lead the wayShow them all the beauty they possess inside, give them a sense of pride to make it easier’
For me, Reception and Early Years is the foundation of most children’s lives, which is why I am the link governor for Early Years. I am proud of how Grove Road goes the extra mile in to make the school inclusive, encourages children to be creative and ensures that all children have the best possible start in life, not just in education but also in being good citizens.
I bring 20 years of marketing and 10 years of procurement skills, mostly in large corporations. This allows me to have critical but constructive insights into the children’s progression, and ask the question, ‘What can we do to improve outcomes?’
In addition, I also volunteer at Hounslow Gurdwara, where I sit on the committee, looking at upgrading the infrastructure.
Catrin Evans – Co-Opted Governor
Catrin grew up in West Wales where her parents were both teachers at local education authority schools. They inspired her to join the Board and being passionate about our wonderfully diverse Grove Road School community. Catrin has been a proud Londoner since the age of 18. She has worked tirelessly in the London community, which has included being a community outreach worker in Notting Hill at the time of the Grenfell Tower tragedy. Passionate about Equity, Diversity and Inclusion, Catrin has volunteered extensively as mentor, hospice volunteer, recovery worker with Mind, and as a bereavement counsellor within diverse London communities. Her career in agile project management within data, tech, Science, Health and AI has spanned working at the London Ambulance Service, Guy’s & St Thomas’ NHS Foundation Trust, The Alan Turing Institute and currently within Data for Science and Health at Wellcome.
Catrin is extremely proud to be School Governor at Grove Road and is committed to our school’s vision and culture, being part of our beautifully diverse School Community, our ambitious School Development Plan, and collaborating to achieve together.
Catrin is proudly neurodiverse. She holds a BMus from the Royal Academy of Music, BSc in Psychology from The Open University, and an MPhil from the University of Cambridge. Catrin is STEM Governor and enjoys working alongside the talented Board of Governors, Mrs Beckford, School leadership, Miss Johnson, Hounslow colleagues, and all the teachers, staff and pupils at Grove Road, to provide robust visible governance and shape the future direction of travel. Catrin is proud to have been a part of the first cohort of ‘Success on the Board’ (Advance HE & Wellcome), which is a development programme targeted at people from groups currently underrepresented on governing bodies.
Barinder Sandhu – Co-Opted Governor
Hello, my name is Barinder. I am a co-opted governor and I started in the post in September 2024. I am a retired lecturer, my career has been in education. Currently I am a volunteer at a local place of worship as head of education.
I am excited to get involved and ensure our children have the best possible learning experience and environment – a place where their creativity, potential and knowledge can thrive and where we can develop skills and friendships that will last a lifetime.
Idris Bora – Parent Governor
I joined the governing body to gain greater insight into school operations and to support positive change in an evolving educational environment.Professionally, I work in product marketing management, bringing a strategic and collaborative approach to my role as a governor.I have two children in primary education and, through both personal and professional experience; I have a strong interest in supporting high-quality education and outcomes for all pupils.
Baldeep Kaur – Parent Governor
We are currently looking for a co-opted governor to join the board. Please contact the office to find out more.

Staff
Senior Leadership Team
Grace Beckford – Headteacher
It feels like a very long time ago, when I graduated from Roehampton University in 2009 with a BA in Primary Education. I have been working at Grove Road since 2011, where before being the Headteacher, I taught many different year groups. I have always loved being a part of the Grove Road family and enjoy learning in a fun, creative way. I love being able to spend time working with all of the teachers and children to make Grove Road the best school it can be.
2023 was an exciting year for me, as it was the year that I stepped into the role of Headteacher, having been the Deputy Headteacher since 2019. Every day is a pleasure – I tell everyone I meet about our special, family school and what an honour it is to now serve as Headteacher.
My husband and I live in Sunbury and enjoy holidays and visiting places of interest when we can. I also love reading, writing a journal and spending time with my family – I have a nephew and two nieces that always make me smile.
Ms Alex Turner – Deputy Headteacher & Indigo Class Teacher
I was delighted to join the team at Grove Road in January 2024 and have been made to feel so welcome by the school community. I graduated from the Institute of Education in 2007, but before this I volunteered in special schools, taught English in primary schools in France and worked as a secondary French teacher in an independent school. I have worked in schools in Hounslow since qualifying as a teacher, and have been a class teacher, early literacy specialist teacher, SENCo, Assistant Headteacher and Deputy Headteacher. My passions in education are music, French, early literacy and positive behaviour. Outside of school, I love to perform in and watch musical theatre, visit historical places with my family and read lots of books with my cat on my lap.
Jenny Johnson – Inclusion Leader & Rainbow Class Teacher
I have been working at Grove Road Primary School since 2011, where my teaching career began in Year 2, after gaining a B Ed (Hons) from the University of Chester. Since being at Grove Road, I have enjoyed working with many wonderful children, staff and parents whilst being responsible for PSHE, RE, English and being a member of the Arts team. I have been fortunate enough to teach across many of the year groups in all three of the Key Stages. Each year group brings new and interesting opportunities whilst learning about a range of topics so I don’t think that I could pick a favourite. As Rainbow class teacher, I am enjoying seeing the children explore and learn through a wide range of experiences across the curriculum as they begin their learning journey. I am a firm believer that you are never too old to learn and I have enjoyed looking for exciting and interesting courses and learning opportunities for staff as part of my role as CPD lead so that we are equipped with the most up to date knowledge and techniques to help our children shine. In my spare time I love reading, shopping, spending time with my family and friends and enjoying a range of food from different cuisines.
Paul Hume – Orange Class Teacher and EYFS & KS1 Leader
With 18 years of teaching experience, I’ve had the joy of working across different roles, including KS1 Lead and Deputy Headteacher of a small independent school. My passion lies in curriculum development and assessment, ensuring that learning is both engaging and effective for every child.
Outside the classroom, you’ll often find me running or diving into a good horror novel—because nothing beats a thrilling story! I love creating a fun, supportive environment where children can flourish and develop a love of learning.
Hayley Glenister – Gold Class Teacher and KS2 Phase Leader
I am thrilled to be a part of the incredible team at Grove Road Primary School. My teaching journey began in 2018, after I successfully completed a PGCE with a PE Specialism at St Mary’s University. Several years into my teaching career, I pursued my Master’s Degree from the Open University, graduating in 2023, focusing on inclusion in the classroom and curriculum. I have had the privilege of teaching in various schools, which has equipped me with invaluable experiences and knowledge that I now apply in my current practice.
Having taught across Key Stage 1 and 2, I am deeply passionate about promoting equality and inclusion. I am dedicated to creating a neurodiverse-friendly classroom where every child feels respected, supported, and empowered to succeed. Central to my teaching philosophy is a commitment to pupil mental well-being, which I view as fundamental to a child’s overall development. I strive to create a safe and nurturing space where students feel confident expressing themselves and growing.
Outside of school, I lead a busy life as a mum of two teenage boys who keep me on my toes. I’m also an animal lover, sharing our home with cats, rabbits, guinea pigs, and fish. In my free time, I indulge in my love for books and movies, with a particular fondness for Harry Potter and Marvel films. I also enjoy the movie Inside Out, including the new one! I am slowly ticking off my bucket list of musicals, with The Lion King and Mrs Doubtfire being particular favourites.
Teaching Staff
Gagan Panesar – Red Class Teacher
I graduated with a Bachelor’s degree in Psychology but then I followed my true passion – working with children! I completed my PGCE in 2017, specialising in Early Years, and have since worked in a variety of schools across Hounslow and beyond.
Early Years is definitely where my heart is! I love being part of the very beginning of a child’s school journey, helping them build those all-important foundations in reading, writing, numeracy and social skills. Watching their confidence, independence and little personalities blossom is one of the most rewarding parts of my job!
Outside of school, I’m a busy mum of three, a big coffee lover and love travelling and exploring new countries with my family. I also have a creative side and run my own balloon and floral décor business, creating special setups for everything from birthdays and baby showers to weddings – often with my three little assistants in tow!
I’m so excited to be part of the Grove Road family and can’t wait for all the fun, learning, laughter and wonderful memories ahead!
Jemima Briscombe – Yellow Class Teacher
I have had 4 years of experience in a wide range of schools and am really enjoying my first year at Grove Road! I have a teaching degree which I completed in Worcester, where I am from. I love being part of the learning journey for children, instilling knowledge, creativity and curiosity. I have a passion for reading and endeavour to inspire children to find the pleasure and magic in reading.
Outside of school, I love painting, walking and a good film! Having only moved to London a year ago, I am enjoying exploring all the wonders the busy city has to offer.
Miss Aoife McGarrity – Green Class Teacher
Hi! I am Miss McGarrity. I love reading, doing mindfulness and colouring during my spare time. I also love watching Gaelic football. I enjoy travelling and going back to my home country Ireland to visit all my family. My favourite food by far is pasta!
I am enjoying teaching at Grove Road- especially being with Green Class and meeting all the Grove Road family. I can’t wait to experience the many trips and celebrations throughout the year, especially Taste of Grove Road.
Hina Chaudhary – Blue Class Teacher

I graduated from the University of West London with a Bachelor of Music degree. My passion for music and singing began at the age of three and has never left me! I pursued my career as a professional musician and performer with great dedication and enthusiasm, while also teaching privately for many years.
My journey into education developed further when I joined an independent prep school, where I discovered a love for teaching a wide range of subjects. This inspired me to become a qualified primary teacher, gaining my qualification while working at an outstanding all-through school in Hounslow. During my many years there, I had the opportunity to develop my practice and flourish in a variety of roles, including Primary Music Lead and, later, Director of Music.
I am thrilled to be back at Grove Road, where I completed my teaching placement a few years ago, and to now be part of such a welcoming team and wonderful school community.
I absolutely love working with children of all ages and helping them develop the skills, confidence and self-belief to become whatever they aspire to be. I believe in high expectations, exemplary behaviour and commitment, while creating an environment in which children feel inspired to learn and achieve their very best.
Outside school, you can usually find me enjoying nature, animals and books , while running after my two and a half year old son! Of course, I still love to sing and perform and continue to share the joy of music at every opportunity. My little one can certainly confirm this, as he practically sings in his sleep too!
Matthew Elgar – Violet Class Teacher
I graduated from Kingston University London in 2016 with a First Class degree in Primary Education with Mathematics specialism. I have taught across Key Stage 1 and Key Stage 2 in Hounslow, Richmond, Spain and Japan. After teaching at an international school in Tokyo for two years, I was drawn to Grove Road by its warm atmosphere and strong sense of community.
One of the things I love most about teaching is seeing the moment when something finally clicks for a child. I also enjoy getting to know the unique personalities in my class and helping children feel happy, confident and ready to learn. I believe children do their best learning when they feel calm, supported and listened to.
Outside of school, I enjoy travelling, learning languages and exploring different cultures. I also love films and theatre, trying new foods and planning my next adventure.

I started a childcare course at Kingston college in 2019 for 2 years. In 2020, I spent my time here at Grove Road completing a student placement with the EYFS team. The staff here are so welcoming and made me feel comfortable not only to work with but to support my confidence in my course I was doing. I enjoyed it so much here I decided to apply to work here. Mr. Tyrone Polius – Centre TA
My name is Tyrone Polius. I started working at Grove Road Primary in March 2024 as a teaching assistant. I realised I had an interest in working with children when I used to do youth work at the weekends, doing various activities with children of different ages. I believe working at Grove Road has helped me develop and learn some new skills. Ive also enjoyed my time there so far working with other members of staff, helping children reach their potential. I also find it rewarding having the opportunity to see the children progress.
Ashwini Deshmukh – Centre TA
Hello! I’m Mrs Ashwini Deshmukh and I have been working with Grove Road Primary School since January 2026. Harpinder Kaur – SEN TA
I started working at Grove Road Primary School in 2025 as a SEN Teaching Assistant. The staff here are very welcoming. Its’s a pleasure working with such a talented and supportive team. I’m grateful for all the support and encouragement. I always wanted to be a Teaching Assistant, as I enjoy working with children. I would describe myself as an open and honest person. My greatest strength is my patience and adaptability.
In my free time I like to go for long walks, enjoy travelling, shopping and spending quality time with my family.

SEN at Grove Road
Special Educational Needs
We strive to offer a happy, safe, caring and secure school in a setting where teamwork, high standards of work and behaviour are the norm, effort is valued and where positive attitude to all school life is developed. We will endeavour to provide a broad, balanced, relevant, differentiated and accessible curriculum for each pupil irrespective of their ability, race, gender, background or beliefs: in order to promote physical, intellectual, spiritual, moral, aesthetic and cultural development so as to prepare the children for positive and successful futures.
We believe in equality of opportunity and we aim to create a supportive yet challenging environment that values difference and recognises the achievements of all children. We acknowledge the importance of strong links between school, home and community and continue to work on strengthening these connections.
Provision
At Grove Road Primary all of our children are individuals and, as such, they have a range of strengths and needs. We aim to include all children, including those with additional needs, in every aspect of school life.
We work in collaboration with a range of external agencies including Speech Therapists, Occupational Therapists, Educational Psychologists as well as many others to ensure that our children receive the best possible support available. We aim to identify difficulties early and provide the appropriate intervention in order to help children make good progress. When children come into the Nursery or Reception classes, we carry out a language monitoring. This helps us to identify which children may need some extra support with developing their language skills. Identified children then take part in group work led by our Specialist Teaching Assistants before being assessed again to see how much progress they have made.
We also deliver a wide range of interventions across the school, within the classroom as well as in small groups or 1:1 settings aimed at improving children’s literacy, maths or social skills. Parents of children with special educational needs are encouraged to talk to us in school and to share ideas with each other.
If you would like to speak to our SENCo, Miss Jenny Johnson, please use the email rainbow@groveroad.hounslow.sch.uk

Nursery
Admission criteria for Nursery
Children are eligible for a free, part-time Nursery place the September before their fourth birthday. For entry in September 2025, the child’s date of birth will be between 1.9.2022 and 31.8.2023. Children born between 1.9.2023 and 31.8.2024 will be eligible for September 2027 entry.
All Hounslow’s infant and primary schools have Nursery classes and enquiries and applications for a Nursery place should be made direct to the individual schools.
When making your application, you will need to consider carefully the admissions process and the oversubscription criteria.
If a Nursery receives more applications than it has to offer, the places will be offered strictly in accordance with the London Borough of Hounslow’s oversubscription criteria, which are available on Hounslow’s website, www.hounslow.gov.uk.
Application forms can be obtained from the school office, downloaded below or from the London Borough of Hounslow’s admissions department. It is very important to make sure you return the form to the school by the deadline. Late applications severely limit your chances of receiving the school of your choice. The address you provide must be the address at which your child normally resides and you will need to provide proof of address along with your application. It is a criminal offence to give a false address and the school reserves the right to withdraw any offer made on the basis of inadequate or deliberately misleading information.
At Grove Road Primary School we have a morning Nursery with 26 places, which runs five mornings a week, Monday to Friday from 9am – 12pm.
Please contact the school on 020 8570 6132 or email office@groveroad.hounslow.sch.uk for help with application forms or any other information and we will be pleased to help.
The over-subscription criteria for Nursery Education in September 2025 are:
Looked after children and children who have been adopted (or made subject to a residence order or special guardianship) immediately following having been looked after.
Applicants whose child’s medical or social circumstances require attendance at a particular school rather than any other school. In such cases parents are reminded that they must complete the appropriate section on the application form and attach a supporting statement from a suitable professional such as a consultant or a social worker.
Applicants who will have a son or daughter, including all blood, half-, step-, adoptive and foster brothers and sisters of the child (not cousins) who live at the same home as the child, in the infant, linked junior or primary school in September 2025. This would not apply if the sibling were due to leave in the July before the younger child would be admitted.
Where there are more applications that meet this criterion than there are places in the school, priority will then be given to those children who live nearest to the school, with the distance from home to school being measured as set out in the note below. *
Priority will then be given to children living in the London Borough of Hounslow within the Priority Admission Area.
Where there are more applications that meet this criterion than there are places in the school, priority will then be given to those children who live nearest to the school, with the distance from home to school being measured as set out in the note below. *
Priority will then be given to children living in the London Borough of Hounslow, outside the Priority Admission Area.
Where there are more applications that meet this criterion than there are places in the school, priority will then be given to those children who live nearest to the school, with the distance from home to school being measured as set out in the note below. *
Where there are more applications that meet this criterion than there are places in the school, priority will then be given to those children who live nearest to the school, with the distance from home to school being measured as set out in the note below. *
* Distance will be measured by computer software based on Ordnance Survey and postal address data. The software measures using public roads and footpaths adopted and recorded by Hounslow Council’s Highways Team. When using roads for measurement purposes the software measures along the middle of the road. It starts from a point in the footprint of the property provided as the child’s address and continues by the shortest available route to the nearest of the school gates which is used by pupils to enter the school grounds. Blocks of flats are treated as one address. In blocks of flats, priority will normally be given to the lowest flat number. Addresses in private roads will measure from the footprint of the property, along the middle of the private road leading to the public road/footpath as adopted and recorded by Hounslow Highways Team. Not used are routes using common land1, open spaces, public parks, subways or footpaths not adopted by the Highways team2.
In the event that the distances are equal, the school will draw lots to determine which applicant should be offered the place.
Note: Maps of the catchment areas will be available from the Council, infant and primary schools and libraries.
Parents should note that admission to Reception classes is determined using the admission criteria for primary schools. Attendance at a nursery does not guarantee a Reception place at the attached infant or primary school. ADMISSION TO THE INFANT OR PRIMARY SCHOOL FROM THE NURSERY IS THEREFORE NOT AUTOMATIC AND CANNOT BE GUARANTEED.

Reception
The Reception class is the first class of the main school. Children join when they are four, the September before their fifth birthday.
All Reception class applications must be made using your home Local Authority’s common application form (CAF) and should be submitted to your Local Authority. You can apply for up to six schools on one application form, which should be listed in order of preference and you are advised to use all six preferences. Your preferences will be considered under an equal preference system; i.e. all preferences are considered separately, regardless of their ranking on your form, therefore, if your application is successful for more than one school, you will offered a place at the school you ranked highest on your CAF.
When considering your preferences, you will need to consider carefully the admissions process and the oversubscription criteria. If a school receives more applications than the number of places it has to offer, the places will be offered in accordance with the London Borough of Hounslow’s oversubscription criterion, which is available on Hounslow’s website,www.hounslow.gov.uk.
You can apply online or on a paper CAF form (which can be obtained from schools or from your Local Authority’s admissions department). If you apply online, you will receive notification of the result of your application via email the day before parents who have applied on paper, who will be notified by post.
It is extremely important to ensure that you return your application form by the deadline. Late applications severely limit your chances of gaining a place for your child at your preferred school.
The address you provide on the application form must be the address at which the child normally resides and you will need to provide proof of address along with your application. It is a criminal offence to give a false address and the Local Authority / school reserves the right to withdraw any offer made on the basis of inadequate, inaccurate or deliberately misleading information.
Each year we hold open mornings for prospective parents, when parents are invited to look round the school, meet the Headteacher and other teaching staff, collect application forms and related documents, as well as ask any questions about the school or the admissions process.
Please telephone the school on 020 8570 6132 or email office@groveroad.hounslow.sch.uk for details of open mornings, CAF application forms or for any other information.
1. Looked after children (as defined in the Children Act 1989) or a child who was previously looked after and has left care under a Child arrangements order, special guardianship order or who was adopted. (See page 4 in the Starting school in Hounslow brochure for further information)
2. Exceptional Medical/Social need – Applicants whose child’s medical or social circumstances require attendance at a particular school rather than any other school. (See page 4 in the Starting school in Hounslow brochure for further information)
3. Sibling – Children who will have a brother or sister, including all blood half-, step-, adoptive and foster brothers and sisters of the child (not cousins) who live at the same home as the child, in the infant, linked junior or primary school in September 2026. This would not apply if the sibling were due to leave in the July before the younger child would be admitted.
4. Children of staff – children of any member of staff, regardless of role in the school where;
a) The member of staff has been directly employed by the school for two or more years at the time of application or
b) The member of staff is recruited to fill a vacant post for which there is a demonstrable skill shortage
5. Distance – Where there are more applications that meet this criterion than there are places in the school, priority will be given to those children who live nearest to the school, with the distance from home to school being measured using a computerised mapping system.
For all schools where the Local Authority (LA) is the Admissions Authority (AA) for the school and any schools where the Admissions Authority (the Governing Body or Academy Trust) has a policy to use the LA’s measuring system, the walking route is measured by using a geographical information system.
It starts from a “seed point” which is a point of measurement in the footprint of the home address. The seed point is provided by the Local Land and Property Gazetteer (LLPG) from information compiled by the Local Authority or from the National Land Property Gazetteer (NLPG) for addresses outside our borough.
From the seed point, the route firstly connects to the nearest node of the digitised network. It will always measure using the centre of the road nearest to this point even if your home address is on the corner of two roads. The positioning of front doors, driveways and back gates are not relevant to the route or the measurement and are not programmed to be used by the measuring system. The digitised network is constructed from road data supplied by Ordnance Survey called OS Master map Highways Network. OS Master map Highways Network has been accurately digitised to measure along the centre of the road; the LA has no control over how OS digitise the road and footpath network.
The network starts from the seed point in the property provided as the child’s address and continues by the walking route to the nearest of the school gates which is used by pupils to enter the school grounds. Where there are multiple applications with equal distances, the LA’s database will randomly order these.
The walking route is established using an algorithm within the software used by the LA. This programme integrates with the LA’s database (Synergy/School Admissions Management) which is supplied by Access UK Ltd (www.theaccessgroup.com)
Other measuring systems may give a different measurement, but the Local Authority cannot take a measurement from another measuring system.
If there is one place available and two or more children next in order of priority or next on the waiting list meet the appropriate criterion equally, the place will be allocated using the distance criterion.
Parents should note that admission to Reception classes is determined using the admission criteria for primary Schools. Attendance at a nursery does not guarantee a Reception place at the attached infant or primary school.
ADMISSION TO THE PRIMARY SCHOOL FROM THE NURSERY IS THEREFORE NOT AUTOMATIC AND CANNOT BE GUARANTEED.

pageCache.text:
ASC Centre
Criteria for Admission
General Description of Need:
This Centre is for children with long-term difficulties in the autistic spectrum affecting their access to the curriculum. There should be involvement from agencies including educational psychology, and CAMHS or the Child Development Team, confirming a description of ASC.
Cognition/Ability Range:
Children between 4-11 years with an ability within the broad average range. They may present with an uneven cognitive profile.
There should be evidence that the child’s autistic spectrum condition is affecting their learning so that the child is likely to need additional support in curriculum subjects for some of the time.
There should be a need for a differentiated curriculum, adjusted for the child’s particular type of learning style.
There should be evidence that the child is able to learn visually.
The child should be able to manage the demands of a mainstream environment with some support where necessary and should be able to manage some independent learning.
The child should be able to benefit from a balance of mainstream and small group teaching.
There should be evidence that the child is able to learn with mainstream peers.
The child could have difficulties with communication such as: limited non-verbal or pre-verbal communication skills, difficulties with verbal comprehension, understanding abstract language and non-literal language, restricted, unusual use of language.
Spoken language should be the child’s main method of communication.
The child needs regular support from a speech and language therapist working alongside skilled school staff to develop their communication skills and/or use of language.
The child could have difficulties with social interaction such as: not initiating or avoiding contact with others, inappropriate social and emotional behaviour.
The child could need regular specialist support to develop their social understanding and social skills.
The child could have difficulties with thinking and behaviour such as: restricted imagination and inflexible thinking such as repetitive rather than imaginative play, fixed or limited areas of interest, difficulty coping with unplanned change.
There could be evidence that the child’s autistic spectrum condition is affecting their social and emotional development such that it is causing anxiety or social problems.
The child should have broadly age appropriate self-help skills (in relation to toileting, feeding etc.)
The child is able to manage in a mainstream school with little to no support.
The child shows more significant difficulties indicating that they are likely to need a greater input or more intensive specialist support.
Please discuss placement with your caseworker or current school in the first instance.
We have a monthly, adults-only open afternoon for parents wishing to consider our Centre. Please contact the school office to book a place.
